terra.problem: Calling Kiriath-jearim a mouthful jokes about how a Bible name is said.
Saying the gap is where the trouble starts overlooks the grief and violence already described.
The shortage is stated in verse 14, not the next verse, verse 13.
“I won't joke here” comments on how Papa tells the passage.
A yearly feast does not establish that everyone knows when and where to look.
The passage does not say Shiloh is already full of people.
The elders anticipate a complaint from fathers or brothers; the passage does not say they actually show up or complain.
Judges 20:48 says cities in the path of the men of Israel were burned, not cities in Benjamin's path. The new kitchens are also an invented detail about the Bible event.
Judges 20:48 says the men of Israel burned cities in their path; it does not establish that all the cities the Benjamites rebuilt had been burned.
The passage says the Israelites returned home, not that there were no more assemblies.
